Projects

Five projects, newest first
Sep 2025 – May 2026 · Senior capstone

Hoffman EV Chassis Optimization

My team’s goal was a 20% weight reduction on Hoffman EV’s existing chassis for an electric pickup truck built on the Tesla platform. I redesigned the front subframe mount (Fig. 1) and the side rail assembly (Fig. 2) to integrate with Tesla components and pass the NHTSA standard for side impact.

  • SolidWorks sheet metal
  • SolidWorks FEA
  • SolidWorks topology optimization
Sep 2025 – May 2026

Baja SAE Carbon Fiber Seat

My biggest goal as a second-year team lead on Baja SAE was to upgrade our long-unchanged sheet metal seat to a carbon fiber bucket seat. I selected materials, carried out a key redesign of the seat 3D model (Fig. 3), adapted the design for molding, and led fabrication and implementation (Fig. 4a) of the seat.

  • SolidWorks surface modeling
  • SolidWorks FEA
  • Carbon fiber wet layup
  • Leadership & communication
Sep 2022 – May 2024

Baja SAE Carbon Fiber Hood

A new hood design was my first project as a freshman on Baja, and I carried it to completion the next year as team lead. I iteratively redesigned the hood for mud deflection and self-taught CFD (Fig. 5) to analyze how the new hood would keep our driver clean. The following year, I directed and carried out resin infusion of the new hood (Fig. 6).

  • SolidWorks 3D modeling
  • SolidWorks CFD
  • Carbon fiber resin infusion
  • Leadership & communication
Sep 2023 – Dec 2023

D.I.R.E.C.T. Cryovial Transfer System

My first group project at UW–Madison was designing a product for a research client that could pick up a row of cryovials, adjust their spacing, and insert them into a different package. Our solution is a small handheld device. One hand adjusts vial spacing with the lime green handle while the other hand works the magenta clamping mechanism (Fig. 7). I created the 3D model of our solution and directed prototyping (Fig. 8).

  • SolidWorks 3D modeling
  • Client communication
  • Prototyping
